svg.title: Federated Ummah infrastructure: governance, trust layer, four purpose-built sites and public logs
svg.desc: Title: “Many purpose-built sites, one trust layer, every action logged in public”. A sketch of shared Ummah infrastructure, drawn from EuroHPC, CERN, X-Road and Gaia-X. At the top, two boxes. Governance: shura council, with governments, sovereign funds and civil society, and capacity split by a written formula (MoU). Funding: a waqf endowment (corpus kept, yield runs it), with sukuk and sovereign anchors funding the build. Both point down to the shared trust layer (X-Road style): member registry, certificates, open standards; no central data store. The trust layer connects to four purpose-built sites, each on a certified open stack with attested hardware: DPI hosting (ID, payments, exchange); AI compute (pooled training, merit); Records registry (waqf, zakat, archives); Backup site (treaty-protected copy). Each site publishes to public, append-only logs that anyone can verify: Code (reproducible builds, SBOMs, signed releases); Data access (signed message logs, consent records); Money (tenders and contracts in OCDS); Energy (power and water per data centre). Members, scholars, journalists and citizens audit the logs without asking permission (nasihah).
